headline: coiling bases beat plain breakouts by +1.9 points over 3 months, +3.7 when the stock was already 100%+ above its 52-week low
intro: Every signal the scanner would have shown with the app's default settings, recreated bar by bar on NSE daily data from 2005 to 2026 (liquid stocks, ₹1 crore+ a day), and what the stock did next. A Breakout is bought at the next session's open; a Coiling base gets a buy-stop at the pivot for 20 sessions. The stop is the base low and the target twice the risk, exactly as the scanner shows them. Each group is compared with plain breakouts (a first close above the 60-session high) from the same depth below the 6-month high in the same years.

rows.label: Breakout — closed through the pivot on 2.5×+ volume
Coiling — a buy-stop at the pivot for 20 sessions
Breakout, less than 100% above the low
Coiling, less than 100% above the low

findings: The scanner has a real but modest edge. Coiling bases that filled their buy-stop beat plain breakouts by +1.9 points over 3 months (likely +1.4 to +2.4) and rose 20% before falling 8% in 37% of cases against 32%. Breakouts on the day: +1.1 points (+0.4 to +1.8).

The stop is close, so many bases fail first. Only 53% of coiling bases broke out within 20 sessions; the rest broke the base low first. Of the trades taken, 41% reached the 2R target before the stop — at 2-to-1 that still pays (about +0.22R a trade before costs).

Distance above the 52-week low is the biggest lever. At 100%+ above the low the edge roughly doubles: coiling +3.7 points (+2.9 to +4.5), breakouts +2.3; at 150%+ coiling reaches +5.3. Below 100% the edge almost disappears (+0.7 and +0.2). It held in all three periods (2005–12 +4.6, 2013–19 +4.2, 2020–26 +3.3). That is the one change the best tested settings button makes: the low-distance floor goes from 30% to 100%.

The tight base itself adds something. Against plain breakouts from stocks just as strong (Strict trend, within 12% of the high, the same band above the 52-week low, the same years) coiling still added +1.1 points (+0.6 to +1.5), breakouts +0.7 (-0.0 to +1.3).
Grades rank weakly. Grade A is rare (118 breakouts in 21 years); B and C did about the same. Use the grade to sort, not to filter.

No other single setting beat the defaults. Max tightness 3–10%, a 5- or 8-bar minimum base, Standard or Relaxed trend, or 6–40% from the high put coiling between +1.0 and +1.9 points (defaults +1.9); bases of 12+ bars did worst (+0.4).
Weak markets hurt breakouts. With the Nifty 50 below its 200-day average, breakouts rose 20% before falling 8% in 26% of cases (strong market 35%) and hit the stop first 65% of the time.

The extra base types add no clear edge over the flat base. Breakouts from high tight flags (-1.5) and episodic pivots (-1.0) lagged plain breakouts; wedges, cups, Darvas boxes and pocket pivots landed between +0.6 and +2.2. They are there because the app has them — treat their grades as untested ideas.

A textbook contraction sequence (T1 > T2 > T3 before the base) did not add anything (+1.4 points with it, +2.3 without), so the scanner is left exactly as written: the last, tight contraction is what counts.
method: Data: EOD2 NSE daily bars, split- and bonus-adjusted, cleaned with the app's own clean_df; the scanner is the site's JavaScript port, checked against the app's Python on 9,847 signals and 1,500 random non-signal days (identical). One signal per base: a coiling run counts once (first day), breakouts at least 10 sessions apart. Returns are measured against the average liquid NSE stock; the likely range is a month-clustered bootstrap (90%). Costs and slippage are not included. Past results, not a promise.

Breakout|Flat.note: Flat bases 100%+ above the 52-week low did better: +2.3 points.

Coiling|Flat.note: Flat bases 100%+ above the 52-week low did better: +3.7 points.
